spec_match.rationale: Runs native setHTML with the default, a dictionary config {elements:[…],attributes:[]} and a user JSON config in the current spec shape; lanes differ as expected (e.g. img-onerror: default/strict drop img, custom keeps ).

interactive.rationale: Six example buttons, live input/config typing, and re-sanitize all update three lanes plus meters; previews neutralise subresources.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index describes three lanes with editable custom JSON and removal counts, which matches.

edge_cases.rationale: A custom config that allows script/onerror is still stripped by setHTML (good, but unexplained); an invalid config ({elements, removeElements}) makes setHTML throw TypeError and the page silently swaps in its JS walker, showing that output as the custom lane; bad JSON silently becomes {}; strict/custom drop whole <article> content without explaining remove-with-content.

references.rationale: Cites chromestatus.com/feature/5814067399491584 and the WICG spec.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 driven by Node Playwright (chromium.launch) against a local server on :3111 — NOT chrome-devtools-mcp, which is unavailable in this environment, so this is not DevTools-MCP-verified evidence; no accessibility-tree dump was taken. All 6 examples clicked, custom JSON edited (unsafe-allow, invalid, malformed), zero console errors and zero failed requests (preview neutraliser works); 0px overflow both classes.

telemetry_health.rationale: Shared runtime capture only; config TypeErrors are swallowed by an empty catch.

accessibility.rationale: Inputs labelled and buttons native, but lane outputs are not live regions and each lane's code vs visual panes are unlabeled divs.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px overflow both classes; 6 of 9 controls under 44px on mobile.

openQuestions.title: Report config errors instead of falling back to the JS walker
openQuestions.detail:
Repro: custom JSON {"elements":["p"],"removeElements":["img"]} → setHTML throws TypeError, page shows '

x

' from its own walker as the custom result. Show the TypeError in the custom lane; likewise flag JSON parse errors.

openQuestions.title: Explain why setHTML ignores unsafe allowances
openQuestions.detail: Allowing script/onerror in the custom config still yields them stripped; add a note and a setHTMLUnsafe lane so the safe-by-default guarantee is visible rather than surprising.

openQuestions.title: Make removal counts accurate and lanes announced
openQuestions.detail: countRemoved compares elements by index, so attribute counts are approximate; use a structural diff. Add aria-live/role=status to lane outputs.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use setHTML()/Document.parseHTML() with a Sanitizer config of the current shape (elements, attributes, replaceWithChildrenElements); elements not in `elements` are removed with their content; unsafe elements cannot be re-allowed via setHTML.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Followed — current config shape; could add replaceWithChildrenElements to show content-preserving removal.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce asynchronous/changing results through a polite live region (role=status/log or aria-live) and keep controls as native buttons with accessible names.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use intrinsic/grid layouts that collapse to one column at narrow widths (minmax(0,1fr), container/media queries) so no fixed-column track forces horizontal overflow.

summary: The strongest of the four Sanitizer concepts: real setHTML in three lanes with the current config shape and safe preview neutralisation. Its weak spots are swallowed config errors (which fall back to a JS walker that looks native) and missing announcements.
